02 / A sky remembered

A sky that drifts.

A GAN trained on the same 655 cloud frames generates images from latent values. Travel through eight contrasting points and watch the cloud shapes change.

Choose a path through the model
The selected path visits visibly different cloud outputs. Load the model, then start the drift.

Shorter transitions move faster. Range changes the latent values; larger values may distort the image. Every frame comes from the trained generator.

Path anchors
Recorded model output

The same path, rendered smoothly.

A 16-second render of the selected eight-anchor path at 1.0× range. I will use this if live inference is slow. Each frame is a model output; playback runs at 12 frames per second.

About this experiment

Cloud GAN v2 · FastGAN-inspired teaching implementation · 256-dimensional latent vector · spherical interpolation. The original two anchors generated nearly identical outputs. Eight contrasting anchors were selected from 24 tested seeds using image differences, then visually reviewed. The model weights are unchanged. The exported cloud2.onnx model produces an RGB image from a latent vector. Generation runs in this browser; inputs are not sent to an inference service.
